payload.title: Qualify retained Python analysis and lexical-field reuse across real consumers
payload.summary: Priority2 MAINTENANCE investigation. Module declaration lookup parses functions, classes and its own AST; references and per-reference target/facade lookup repeat analysis; Localization validates native facts by replay; ContextTools._reference_analysis reconstructs module interpretations per source; BM25 rebuilds filename evidence per query. Inspect actual multiple-consumer cost before changing computation ownership. Reuse existing performance/retrieval profiler and retained snapshot semantics.
payload.benefit: Acceptance: reproduce parse/index construction counts and elapsed work on at least module/reference resolution and native map preparation or obligation acquisition. Identify minimum exact input closure: retained occurrence/text, grammar/runtime/analyzer version, explicit roots/universe and supported resolution scope. Compare existing behavior and reuse on positive/unsupported/stale/forged/ambiguous cases; preserve identities/order/errors and no external reads. Report whether a local helper, task-scoped memo or no change is justified; no generic source store/cache/graph engine, no speedup from unmeasured asymptotics. Historical performance results remain unchanged.
payload.uncertainty: Some rederivation is security/integrity validation; removing it without exact-frame authentication is unsafe. Different grammar/binding policies must remain distinct. Existing B-0008 broad reuse pressure is related; this qualifies concrete repeated current consumers before implementation. Maintenance-agent investigation possible with bounded deterministic workload, not scientific treatment replay.
